headline: Students join a protest movement in Albania

chunks.text: Thousands of students in Albania, a country in southeastern Europe, have {{risen up}} against the government. From October 13 to 15, 2026, they marched in the capital, Tirana. They are angry about the high cost of education and poor [[job prospects]] after [[graduation]]. They have joined a wider protest called the Flamingo Movement. It {{calls for}} the [[resignation]] of Prime Minister Rama, who has been [[in power]] since 2013. The students are {{taking on}} a leader who has won four national elections.

chunks.text: The movement began months earlier with protests against a resort project. An [[investment company]] linked to the [[son-in-law]] of U.S. President Donald Trump plans to build a [[luxury resort]] on the southern coast. The movement's name comes from protest signs showing flamingos, which live in a [[nature reserve]] near the site. Protesters say the government is {{selling off}} parts of the coast. They say anger over prices, jobs and [[corruption]] had {{built up}} for months. The government [[denies]] the [[allegations]].

chunks.text: On October 14, [[riots]] in Tirana lasted more than eight hours. Groups of young people {{broke away}} from the marches and attacked government buildings, banks and stores. [[Riot police]] used [[tear gas]] and water cannons to {{hold back}} the crowds. Dozens of people were hurt, including many police officers. Organizers accuse the police of {{cracking down}} too hard on protesters and journalists. The next day, smaller [[clashes]] {{broke out}} in other cities.

mainIdea.s: Albanian students angry about school costs and few jobs have joined a movement against the prime minister. The protests turned violent in the capital, but he refuses to resign.
mainIdea.why: Students have risen up over education costs and poor job prospects. The Flamingo Movement calls for Rama's resignation, but he says he will not step down.

mainIdea.s: Thousands of young Albanians are marching because the government closed several universities. The prime minister has agreed to new elections, and the movement is now ending.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the students are angry about high costs and poor job prospects. Rama says he will not step down, and the protests are spreading.

mainIdea.s: Albania has opened a new nature park on its southern coast to protect pink flamingos. Tourists will soon be able to watch the birds from special wooden paths near the water.
mainIdea.why: This is about student protests that call for the prime minister to resign. Protesters say the government is selling off parts of the coast.

lines.text: Did you see the news from Albania? Thousands of students have {{risen up}} against the government.
Students? What are they upset about?
Mostly money. School is expensive, and a lot of young people can't [[make ends meet]].
And finding a good job after college is hard there, right?
Very hard. Some students say [[it's all about who you know]].
So is this just a student protest?
No. They joined the Flamingo Movement, which {{calls for}} the prime minister's resignation.
It started with a plan for a luxury resort linked to Jared Kushner, near a nature reserve full of flamingos. Protesters say the government is {{selling off}} the coast.
So anger {{built up}} over the summer.
Exactly. Then on October 14, some groups {{broke away}} from the marches and attacked buildings.
Wow. Things are really [[out of hand]].
Police used tear gas to {{hold back}} the crowds. Organizers say the police {{cracked down}} too hard.
Protesting is a right, but you have to [[draw the line]] at violence.
The prime minister agrees with that part. But he won't {{step down}}.
Is he at least willing to talk?
He says he's ready to {{sit down}} with students about education costs.
Well, if school costs that much, you can see why they're [[fed up]].
